root_cause_text: The kubelet's container log manager had a fixed 10-second monitoring interval and performed log rotation sequentially, one container at a time. Under very high log generation rates combined with many containers on a node, this caused delays in detecting and rotating logs when size limits were reached, allowing logs to grow excessively large.
fix_summary: Enabled a mechanism for concurrent log rotatation via `kubelet` using a configuration entity of `containerLogMaxWorkers` which controls the maximum number of concurrent rotation that can be performed and an interval configuration of `containerLogMonitorInterval` that can aid is configuring the monitoring duration to best suite your cluster's log generation standards.
fix_pr_title: kubelet: enable configurable rotation duration and parallel rotate
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Current implementation of the `container_log_manager.go` works with the following behavior 

1. It monitors the logs every 10seconds (not configurable)
2. Rotates the logs in a single loop one after the other for each container. 

This behavior causes a few issues with increase in rate at which the containers will start logging. As suggested in #110630 for example where the containers were generating logs at a monumentally high rate of 6M/second. 

Due to the time required to iterate over each container, compress and rotate the files, the log rotation can never really honor the configured value of `container-log-max-files` and `container-log-max-size` on a cluster with this high log generation rate + a large number of such pods running on the cluster. 

##### What this PR does to mitigate this is enable two things. 

1. Enable Parallel log rotation based on a work queue
2. Enable configurable Duration for monitoring the logs for rotation. This can enable a faster more suitable monitoring duration for the logs based on your cluster's log generation capability requirements.

##### How does this PR enable it ?

It adds two additional configuration to the kubelet's configuration parameters

1. `containerLogMaxWorkers`
2. `containerLogMonitorInterval`

One that cater to enable parallel log rotation with a configurable number of workers based on the pod running capacity and the log generation capacity of the cluster and the other to configure how Frequently the logs are monitored and rotated. 

##### How does this work ?

When the container log manager is started off, it creates n equal to `ContainerLogMaxWorkers` number of go routine based workers that are responsible for ensuring the log rotation workflow for the pods in the cluster. A loop running at an interval defined by `ContainerLogMonitorPeriod` lists all the containers and finds out the running containers and pushes that into a Queue. 

This queue is then processed by the worker to rotate the logs.

Currently, there is a wait loop in the tail end to ensure the queue is empty before handing over the control back for the next iteration of the monitoring based on `ContainerLogMonitorPeriod` to avoid the same container getting processed by multiple workers at the same time. 

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #110630

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Enabled a mechanism for concurrent log rotatation via `kubelet` using a configuration entity of `containerLogMaxWorkers` which controls the maximum number of concurrent rotation that can be performed and an interval configuration of `containerLogMonitorInterval` that can aid is configuring the monitoring duration to best suite your cluster's log generation standards.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:
```docs
NA
```


#### Additional Note
I am hoping to get some suggestion on the following

1. I intend to feature gate this so that we can fallback to the old behavior in case if things don't work out as intended. Is there a guidelines for this ? Should there be a KEP first ?
2. This also introduces two new Attributes to the kubelet's configuration parameters. i.e API change. Should this go via the KEP first ?

#### Note to Reviewers
Even with this fix, the log rotation will not be perfect. Considering the fact that we run the log rotation from outside and via a regular interval based lookup, this will work more or less like how the logrotate like infra would do the job. i.e The size of the file can always exceed the max capped size of the log before we actually rotate it via the kubelet. 

The safest way to ensure the rotation of the log as close to the limit as defined in teh config is to setup a notify watch for each log file in question and rotate them. But that can prove to be a really costly operation to be dealt with when the number of containers are really large in size. Also terminating the notify when the pod is deleted or terminated can be an additonal overhead to deal with. But I am happy explore further into that as well if someone thinks that is the better way to rotate and manage the logs.

root_cause_text: The kubelet's orphaned pod volume cleanup logic incorrectly assumed that subpath mounts were always directories and tried to remove them using directory-specific removal methods. However, subpaths can be files (such as sockets or pipes), causing the cleanup to fail when attempting to remove what is not a directory. The code did not account for file subpaths, resulting in deletion failures during cleanup.
fix_summary: Fixed cleanup of Pod volume mounts when a file was used as a subpath.
fix_pr_title: Fix cleanup of file subpaths
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Allow kubelet orphan cleanup to delete both files and empty directories used as subpath mount points.

A pod does not need to use a directory as a subpath, it can use a file (unix domain socket, pipe, ...) too. Therefore the cleanup should use `os.Remove` that deletes both files and empty directories.

This contrasts with whole volumes - a volume is always a directory.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes: #106942

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed cleanup of Pod volume mounts when a file was used as a subpath.
```

```docs

```
evidence: A pod does not need to use a directory as a subpath, it can use a file (unix domain socket, pipe, ...) too. Therefore the cleanup should use os.Remove that deletes both files and empty directories.

root_cause_text: The bug occurs because during kubelet startup with the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled, volumes are reconstructed with a provisional outer volume name before the Pod and API server state is synced. This provisional volume ID is stored indefinitely and used in ActualStateOfWorld, so kubelet cannot correlate the volume with the Pod's expected volume name, causing Pod restart failures after node reboot.

evidence: The node reports in Pod events: Warning  FailedMount ... Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[myvol] ... The reason is that kubelet's VolumeManager reconstructs the volume as uncertain during startup and it uses a provisional outer volume name for it, because it has not seen the API server and Pods in it yet. This provisional volume ID is then used in ActualStateOfWorld forever... While kubelet does mount the volume after reboot, it's not able to match it with the Pod that needs it. Kubelet reports unmounted volumes=[myvol], while the volume is mounted with ID pvc-6357c1ec-bac1-45fd-822f-2d6a014a9721 in my case (= the provisional name, we use PV.name for it) and not myvol (pod.spec.volumes[*].name).

root_cause_text: A recent Kubernetes change intended to avoid autodetecting the node IP when an external cloud provider is used introduced a conditional that inadvertently skipped setting the hostname value from the kubelet. This caused the --hostname-override flag to no longer influence the Node's Addresses.Hostname field. The bug happened because the code returned early before adding the hostname, under the assumption that no node IP meant no host info needed, which was incorrect when a hostname override was present.
fix_summary:
Fixed a regression where `kubelet --hostname-override` no longer worked
correctly with an external cloud provider.
fix_pr_title: Fix behavior with external cloud provider and --hostname-override
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:
#121028 changed kubelet startup to not try to autodetect the node IP when using an external cloud provider, but accidentally also changed it to not write out the kubelet-provided hostname value.

Pre-121028, the `if !nodeIPSpecified { return nil }` wasn't there, so it ended up adding an autodetected node IP and the hostname [below](https://github.com/danwinship/kubernetes/blob/4da16d5c07d82267ada50eca20504a93856a8272/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L233-L236) (whether that hostname was autodetected or overridden). This patch just revises that so we always add the hostname like before, we just don't write out the nodeIP if it wasn't user-specified.

(The 2 unit tests that this changes the behavior of are the 2 that were added in #121028.)

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #124453

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The logic here can be simplified once we drop the legacy cloud provider case, but (a) I wasn't sure what that was waiting for, and (b) this patch needs to be backported anyway.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a regression where `kubelet --hostname-override` no longer worked
correctly with an external cloud provider.
```

root_cause_text: The validation logic for the podLogsDir default path assumed Unix-style paths and did not correctly handle Windows-style path normalization and absolute path checks. This caused the validation to fail on Windows because the default path was not considered absolute or normalized in Windows context.

root_cause_text: The kubelet code did not handle the case where the Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver returns a nil pointer for the NodePrepareResources or NodeUnprepareResources response. Because protobuf encoding can omit empty objects leading to nil pointers, this caused a nil pointer dereference panic in the kubelet.
fix_summary: kubelet no longer crashes when a DRA driver returns a nil as part of the Node(Un)PrepareResources response instead of an empty struct (did not affect drivers written in Go, first showed up with a driver written in Rust).

root_cause_text: The code sets default bind addresses for metrics to the IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.1) regardless of whether the `--bind-address` parameter is configured with an IPv6 address. This results in the metrics listener not using the IPv6 loopback (::1) by default when an IPv6 bind address is configured.

root_cause_text: The data race occurred because concurrent accesses to the PathRecorderMux's internal state (specifically during the ListedPaths call) were not synchronized. This indicates a lack of proper locking or concurrency control around the shared data structures accessed by HTTP handlers, leading to unsafe read/write operations in parallel goroutines.

root_cause_text: The kube-proxy component lacked a properly configured --nodeport-addresses setting in a dual-stack environment, causing it to listen on all IP interfaces (0.0.0.0 and ::) by default. This results in healthCheckNodePort binding to all zeros (wildcard address) instead of a node's specific IP, because the code defaults to listening on all addresses if no specific nodeport address ranges are configured.
fix_summary:
The kube-proxy nodeportAddresses / --nodeport-addresses option now
accepts the value "primary", meaning to only listen for NodePort connections
on the node's primary IPv4 and/or IPv6 address (according to the Node object).
This is strongly recommended, if you were not previously using
--nodeport-addresses, to avoid surprising behavior.

(This behavior is enabled by default with the nftables backend; you would
need to explicitly request `--nodeport-addresses 0.0.0.0/0,::/0` there to get
the traditional "listen on all interfaces" behavior.)
fix_pr_title: Add `--nodeport-addresses primary`, warn on empty `--nodeport-addresses`
fix_pr_body:
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
1. Adds `kube-proxy --nodeport-addresses primary`, which tells kube-proxy to only listen for NodePort connections (and HealthCheckNodePort connections) on the node's primary IP(s)
2. Adds a warning at kube-proxy startup if you pass no `--nodeport-addresses`
3. Adds a warning at kube-proxy startup if you pass a single-stack `--nodeport-addresses` but appear to have a dual-stack cluster.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #122899
Fixes #111863
(In both cases, that's "fixes" in the sense of "logs a warning if you are experiencing that bug, which we can't actually fix without potentially breaking other users")

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

root_cause_text: The root cause is that enabling the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate causes a default resizePolicy field to be added to pod container specs by the apiserver. The kubelet's logic to detect container spec changes for deciding whether to restart containers hashes the entire container spec, including fields that can be set or mutated by feature gates or defaulting. This causes unnecessary container restarts when the feature gate is toggled, because the spec is seen as changed even though those fields do not require container restarts.
fix_summary: Kubelet will not restart the container when fields other than image in the pod spec change.
fix_pr_title: [kubelet]: fixed container restart due to pod spec field changes
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The kubelet should hash on fields that it consider as mutable for the life of the container. 

This can prevent pod restarts caused by modification of the pod spec default value in the following two situations:
1. If an alpha field that is not defaulted graduates to adding a default in beta, an API server upgrade from alpha->beta will modify this data.
2. If an field is enabled through feature gate, if we disable the gate or enable the gate, the data will also be modified.

According to https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/12326#issuecomment-704469840, we know that pods will be drained when upgrading kubelet, so we can change this mechanism on a minor version boundary.
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #122028 #63814

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

```release-note

```

```docs

```

root_cause_text: The root cause is that the semantic versioning library treats both prerelease (e.g., 'rc' versions) and certain stable versions with numeric prerelease slices as prereleases, causing incorrect ordering comparisons. This leads to stable versions not updating the 'latest' files properly when transitioning from an 'rc' prerelease to a stable release because the comparison logic does not distinguish correctly between prerelease and stable versions.
fix_summary: Fix version comparison in VerifyLatestUpdate
fix_pr_title: Fix version comparison in VerifyLatestUpdate
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

We observed that version markers are not getting updated properly on many occasions which is documented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117115

This issue appears when the version marker is supposed to switch from prerelease (rc) to stable. For example: `v1.28.0-rc.1.9+3fb5377b25ec51` -> `v1.28.0-7+c4e17abb04728e` is not going to happen even though left version is lower than right version.

The reason for that is that both `v1.28.0-rc.1.9+3fb5377b25ec51` and `v1.28.0-7+c4e17abb04728e` are considered as "prereleases" by `blang/semver` library. Version is modeled as:

| Version Part | `v1.28.0-rc.1.9+3fb5377b25ec51` | `v1.28.0-7+c4e17abb04728e` |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------  |
| Major            | 1                                                          | 1                                                     |
| Minor            | 28                                                       | 28                                                  |
| Patch            | 0                                                         | 0                                                    |
| Prerelease   | [rc, 1, 9]                                              | [7]                                                 |
| Build             | 3fb5377b25ec51                              | c4e17abb04728e                        |

Comparing versions includes comparing elements in both prerelease slices and that doesn't behave as we would expect in this case.

Given this logic, we always know that:

- Stable releases are going to have only one element in the `prerelease` slice
- Prereleases are going to have two or three elements in the `prerelease` slice

This can be used when comparing the version to properly switch from prerelease (rc) to stable.

There might be a better approach, but I didn't find such an approach from [the `blang/semver` documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/blang/semver/v4). Unit tests are added to cover various cases and ensure that this still works as expected.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117115

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fix version comparison in VerifyLatestUpdate
```


cc @kubernetes/release-engineering
evidence: Comparing versions includes comparing elements in both prerelease slices and that doesn't behave as we would expect in this case.

root_cause_text: The bug occurred because a grace period override of 0 was used during eviction to force immediate pod termination, but the pod worker logic interpreted a zero override as no override and used the pod's full configured grace period. To enforce immediate eviction, a grace period override of 1 second must be used instead of zero.
fix_summary: Fixes a bug where hard evictions due to resource pressure would let the pod have the full termination grace period, instead of shutting down instantly. This bug also affected force deleted pods. Both cases now get a termination grace period of 1 second.
fix_pr_title: fix grace period used for immediate evictions
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Currently when evicting pods due to resource pressure, or when a pod's storage use has exceeded the configured ephemeral-storage resource limit, we use a grace period override of 0 during eviction which actually ends up allowing the pod's full configured grace period rather than performing an immediate eviction due to the logic [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/227c2e7c2b2c05a9c8b2885460e28e4da25cf558/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L998-L1000)

In order to actually perform an immediate eviction we should instead use a grace period override of 1 in these cases.

This is the same as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119570 but rebased. I don't mind which of these is merged, we just really need this fix.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115819

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
There's a lot of discussion in the original PR around making additional changes to address force-deletes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119570
I am of the same mind as the original author that this PR should remain scoped down to this eviction problem

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixes a bug where hard evictions due to resource pressure would let the pod have the full termination grace period, instead of shutting down instantly. This bug also affected force deleted pods. Both cases now get a termination grace period of 1 second.

```

None

root_cause_text: The StatefulSet controller did not handle the case where a pod remained pending due to its PVC being deleted after the pod deletion. The controller failed to detect the missing PVC and thus did not attempt to recreate it automatically, requiring manual pod deletion to trigger PVC recreation and pod scheduling.
fix_summary: PVCs will automatically be recreated if they are missing for a pending Pod.
fix_pr_title: Automatically recreate PVC for pending STS pod
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?




#### What this PR does / why we need it:
See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113139 for details on the bug. Currently the workaround is to delete the pending pod so that the pvc gets recreated with the pod. But we want to automate this so that we don't need manual intervention.

This change is based on https://github.com/mucahitkurt/kubernetes/commit/1ab4b97b8b63228ea25fc541233df15eb0e3d598

there was some discussion on that change ^ here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74374

If a pod is pending, the code will check the informer for the pod's PVCs and if a PVC is not found, it will recreate it. since it is using the informer, this won't make a call directly to the api server each time to see if a pvc exists. 
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113139

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
I tested this on an AWS cluster, following the error case I described in the issue. It recreated the pvc as expected.

I also created an e2e test for this. It will cordon a node and delete the pod, then delete the pvc. The pvc should then be recreated with my change allowing the pod to be rescheduled.

```release-note
PVCs will automatically be recreated if they are missing for a pending Pod.
```

root_cause_text: The cloud-controller-manager (CCM) resyncs all Load Balancer (LB) services whenever any node transitions between Ready and NotReady states. This causes excessive cloud API calls and LB reconfiguration, especially problematic for ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local services where node state changes are irrelevant if the transitioning nodes do not have endpoints for those services. The CCM lacked logic to skip unnecessary syncs for these services, leading to resource exhaustion and service instability at scale.
fix_summary: Reduce the number of cloud API calls and service downtime caused by excessive re-configurations of cluster LBs with externalTrafficPolicy=Local when node readiness changes (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111539). The service controller (in cloud-controller-manager) will avoid resyncing nodes which are transitioning between `Ready` / `NotReady` (only for for ETP=Local Services). The LBs used for these services will solely rely on the health check probe defined by the `healthCheckNodePort` to determine if a particular node is to be used for traffic load balancing.
fix_pr_title: Avoid re-syncing LBs for ETP=local services
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?






#### What this PR does / why we need it:


This PR reduces the amount of LB re-configurations for ETP=local services by removing the sync completely for any node readiness changes, from the CCM's sync loop. The referenced issue explains the problem in greater detail, so readers are henced directed to that for what concerns the genesis of the problem. A lot has been discussed in this PR and a plan forward has been drafted. The following summarizes the discussion:

- Remove syncs w.r.t node state changes in the CCM in 1.25 (follow up PR, once this merges, is to be expected for remaining node conditions) 
- Maybe / possibly / hopefully backport that to the oldest supported Kube version also supporting ETP=local services
- Have the reported status of the LB HC configured for ETP=local services reflect the node state in 1.25 (also in the form of a follow up PR)
- Write KEP for dealing with transitioning node state for all service LBs. 
-  Kube >= after KEP : remove the sync logic for node state changes for all services and move them to the HC 


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Partially fixes #111539 for ETP=local services, specifically: reduces the amount of cloud API calls and service downtime caused by excessive re-configurations of all cluster LBs as an effect of transitioning node readiness state. 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Reduce the number of cloud API calls and service downtime caused by excessive re-configurations of cluster LBs with externalTrafficPolicy=Local when node readiness changes (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/111539). The service controller (in cloud-controller-manager) will avoid resyncing nodes which are transitioning between `Ready` / `NotReady` (only for for ETP=Local Services). The LBs used for these services will solely rely on the health check probe defined by the `healthCheckNodePort` to determine if a particular node is to be used for traffic load balancing. 
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:


```docs

```
evidence: when a cluster reaches a state where the relation between the amount of LBs and cluster nodes reaches an almost equal amount... the amount of cloud API calls performed by the CCM to sync LBs can become overwhelming for the cloud provider

root_cause_text: The ResourceClaimParametersReference API allows an invalid value in the apiGroup field where an API version string (which contains a '/') is accepted instead of a valid API group name. root_cause_text: A prior bug fix (#119779) introduced extra map queries and creations in the scheduler's findNodesThatFitPod logic, which significantly increased computational overhead and caused a severe performance regression when scheduling many daemonset pods. The underlying cause was inefficient handling and representation of node scheduling statuses in the NodeToStatusMap, resulting in expensive O(n) operations and reduced scheduler throughput.
fix_summary:
Fixes a scheduling performance regression when many nodes exist and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset scheduling)

ACTION REQUIRED: For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
fix_pr_title: [scheduler] absent key in NodeToStatusMap implies UnschedulableAndUnresolvable
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#119779 fixed a bug, but caused a performance regression #124709 observed at 5k nodes. Performance fix #124714 was merged, with modest improvement in performance. We still observe reduced throughput when running a test (15k nodes, 60k daemonset pods)

baseline (pre #119779): ~470 pods/s
current (with #124714): ~70 pods/s
[more perf engineering](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/4ca6449890f15ffebcf231456526a15ef37f0d84): ~300 pods/s
**this change:  ~460 pods/s**

This fix attempts to bring us back to baseline performance. We revert #124714, and part of #119779. We implement [option 2 proposed here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/124709#issuecomment-2096605264). While there are two unaddressed O(n) operations ([1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/268919df1a57a6eebe3ac0e27500cbbde2830546/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L460), [2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/268919df1a57a6eebe3ac0e27500cbbde2830546/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L488)), these haven't revealed themselves as performance problems in the wild. To keep this diff as small as possible for cherry-pick, we will defer the fix of those to a future minor version. This future change will require a breaking change to the NodeToStatusMap type, to allow better than O(n), or at least really fast O(n), representation of many nodes with the same status.

pair @mskrocki 


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #124709

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixes a scheduling performance regression when many nodes exist and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset scheduling)

ACTION REQUIRED: For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
```
evidence: #119779 added some map queries and creations that add non-negligible latency.

root_cause_text: On Windows, the container log file was opened without the FILE_SHARE_DELETE flag, causing the file rename operation (log rotation) to fail because the file was locked by the process following the log. The default Go method for opening files did not include this flag, preventing log rotation while the logs were being followed.
fix_summary: Fixed issue where following Windows container logs would prevent container log rotation.
fix_pr_title: windows: Fixes following container log rotation
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?







#### What this PR does / why we need it:

If we're following a file, that file will remain open, and we continue to read data from it when new data becomes available.

On Windows, this can be an issue if the container logs needs to be rotated. Log rotation is done by renaming the file, but this action may fail if the file is already opened.

Setting the ``FILE_SHARE_DELETE`` flag when opening the file will prevent this issue, as documented: ``"Delete access allows both delete and rename operations"`` [1].

In golang, there's no way to set this flag [2], the ``sharemode`` is always set to: ``sharemode := uint32(FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE)``

Thus, we need to open the file ourselves with the right flags.

[1] https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilea?redirectedfrom=MSDN
[2] https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.22.2:src/syscall/syscall_windows.go;l=366

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #124443
Related: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/51540

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed issue where following Windows container logs would prevent container log rotation.
```

root_cause_text: The bug was caused because optional fields in the PodFailurePolicyRule object, such as OnExitCodes, were not marked with 'omitempty' in their struct definitions. fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?





#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #126040

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

My procedure for testing (repro):
0. repro by creating Jobset with Job template embedding the snippet:
```yaml
        podFailurePolicy:
          rules:
          - action: FailJob
            onPodConditions:
            - type: DisruptionTarget
          - action: Ignore
            onExitCodes:
              operator: In
              values: [ 42 ]
```
In results in the following errors:
```sh
> k create -f jobset.yaml
The JobSet "failurepolicy-abcdef" is invalid: 
* spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[0].onExitCodes: Invalid value: "null": spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[0].onExitCodes in body must be of type object: "null"
* spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[1].onExitCodes.containerName: Invalid value: "null": spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[1].onExitCodes.containerName in body must be of type string: "null"
* spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[1].onPodConditions: Invalid value: "null": spec.replicatedJobs[0].template.spec.podFailurePolicy.rules[1].onPodConditions in body must be of type array: "null"
* <nil>: Invalid value: "null": some validation rules were not checked because the object was invalid; correct the existing errors to complete validation
```
1. Build JobSet using the updated `k8s.io/api`: 
- clone `https://github.com/kubernetes/api` into JobSet repo  under `bin/k8s_api/api`, and checkout the `release-1.29` branch
- make code adjustments as in this repro (adding "omitempty")
- adjust JobSet's `go.mod` with `replace k8s.io/api => ./bin/k8s_api/api` to use the code, and adjust its Dockerfile with new line `replace k8s.io/api => ./bin/k8s_api/api`, then `go mod tidy`
- build JobSet image with `make kind-image-build`
- load the image to kind: `kind load docker-image gcr.io/k8s-staging-jobset/jobset:0b8c19c-dirty --name kind`
- adjust the JobSet image for the running deployment with `kubectl edit deploy/jobset-controller-manager -njobset-system`
2. The JobSet creation succeeds, the `kubectl get job -oyaml` returns the correct snippet:
```yaml
    podFailurePolicy:
      rules:
      - action: FailJob
        onPodConditions:
        - status: "True"
          type: DisruptionTarget
      - action: Ignore
        onExitCodes:
          containerName: null
          operator: In
          values:
          - 42
```
(same snippet is created when creating the Job directly, without JobSet)

I have also confirmed that it only matters which version of k8s API is used to build the JobSet. In particular, when used fixed version to build JobSet, then I was able to create JobSets on 1.26 and 1.27 k8s clusters.

I see we did similar fixes in the past like here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121000/

root_cause_text: The bug happened because the server-side apply merge strategy for the ServiceBackendPort struct was not set to 'atomic'. fix_summary:
Changed how the API server handles updates to `.spec.defaultBackend` of Ingress objects.
Server-side apply now considers `.spec.defaultBackend` to be an atomic struct.  This means that any field-owner who sets values in that struct (they are mutually exclusive) owns the whole struct. For almost all users this change has no impact; for controllers that want to change the default backend port from number to name (or vice-versa), this makes it easier.
fix_pr_title: Make ServiceBackendPort an atomic struct
fix_pr_body:
This allows different actors to force ownership of one field without having to explicitly unset the other field.

See #125869

Before: `The Ingress "myingress" is invalid: spec.defaultBackend: Invalid value: "": cannot set both port name & port number`

After: success.

@jpbetz asserts this is safe:  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff/pull/170



Fixes #125869

```release-note
Changed how the API server handles updates to `.spec.defaultBackend` of Ingress objects.
Server-side apply now considers `.spec.defaultBackend` to be an atomic struct.  This means that any field-owner who sets values in that struct (they are mutually exclusive) owns the whole struct. For almost all users this change has no impact; for controllers that want to change the default backend port from number to name (or vice-versa), this makes it easier.
```
evidence: It seems to me that the merge type for the struct ServiceBackendPort should to be set to "atomic"... so that the Operator updating the port should take over the whole struct, and two applications shouldn't update single fields in it.

root_cause_text: The endpoints controller relies on an informer cache to determine the current state of endpoints. When pod states change rapidly, the informer cache can become stale, causing the controller to see outdated endpoint states. Because it perceives the cached state as consistent with the target state, it does not perform necessary updates, resulting in endpoint status being out-of-sync with pod states.
fix_summary: Fix endpoints status out-of-sync when the pod state changes rapidly
fix_pr_title: Fix endpoints status out-of-sync when the pod state changes rapidly
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When Pod state changes rapidly, endpoints controller may use outdated informer cache to sync Service. If the outdated endpoints appear to be expected by the controller, it skips updating it.

The commit fixes it by checking if endpoints informer cache is outdated when processing a service. If the endpoints is stale, it returns an error and retries later.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #125638

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?


root_cause_text: The bug happened because the kube-proxy logic incorrectly removed a check that identified when a UDP endpoint changed from a Serving to a non-Serving state, causing conntrack entries for UDP connections not to be deleted when endpoints were no longer serving. This caused stale conntrack entries to persist after endpoint deletion, leading to failed UDP connections to terminated pods.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Stale UDP endpoint detection got broken in 1.29 as part of #119394; I [incorrectly argued](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119394#discussion_r1313364450) that we could remove an `IsServing()` check, which had the result that now when a UDP endpoint goes from Serving to not-Serving we don't delete the conntrack entry for it. (We only do so if it goes directly from Serving to non-existent.)

(I'm not sure what I was thinking in the linked comment, but the endpoints maps obviously contain non-serving endpoints, since there wouldn't be any point in having the `IsServing` method if they didn't.)

root_cause_text: The root cause is that when a pod transitions to a terminal state, the container runtime's pod status retrieval does not return the pod IP because it only includes the IP if the sandbox is ready. However, the kubelet maintains a cached pod status that still has the IP, but this cached IP was not propagated properly during status updates triggered by terminating pods. This led to temporary removal of the Pod IP in the pod's status. The fix involved ensuring that the IP stored in the cached pod status is preserved when generating the API pod status for terminated pods.
fix_summary: Fix the bug where PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
fix_pr_title: Fix that PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?




#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Additionally, due to the bug there is one more unnecessary API call sent by Kubelet.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #125370

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: pi
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: pi
        image: howardjohn/shell
        command:
        - bash
        - -c
        - |
          sleep 3
          exit 0
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1
```

Output to `> kubectl get pod -w -ocustom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,IP:.status.podIP | ts "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%.S"`:
before:
```
2024-06-10 09:43:05.083475 NAME       PHASE     IP
2024-06-10 09:43:05.083657 pi-bslsx   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:43:05.087107 pi-bslsx   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:43:05.095358 pi-bslsx   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:43:07.197929 pi-bslsx   Running   10.244.1.21
2024-06-10 09:43:10.203104 pi-bslsx   Running   10.244.1.21
2024-06-10 09:43:11.324259 pi-bslsx   Succeeded   <none>
2024-06-10 09:43:12.208545 pi-bslsx   Succeeded   10.244.1.21
2024-06-10 09:43:12.219699 pi-bslsx   Succeeded   10.244.1.21
```
after fix (note there is no extra API status update):
```
2024-06-10 09:38:16.270212 NAME       PHASE     IP
2024-06-10 09:38:16.270374 pi-xgtw6   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:38:16.275953 pi-xgtw6   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:38:16.283406 pi-xgtw6   Pending   <none>
2024-06-10 09:38:17.954194 pi-xgtw6   Running   10.244.1.20
2024-06-10 09:38:20.960806 pi-xgtw6   Running   10.244.1.20
2024-06-10 09:38:22.130329 pi-xgtw6   Succeeded   10.244.1.20
2024-06-10 09:38:22.974978 pi-xgtw6   Succeeded   10.244.1.20
```
Note that the last status update in both cases is the removal of the Job finalizer.

Some questions potential questions based on my priv chats:
1. why in the broken version the last status update contains the IP?
This is because the last status update is triggered by [`syncTerminatedPod`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/291378cd33cb89342fa876e201030172bb33d3b9/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2161C20-L2161C37) which generates the `apiPodStatus` based on the `podStatus` which is passed from the cache in [pod_workers](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/291378cd33cb89342fa876e201030172bb33d3b9/pkg/kubelet/pod_workers.go#L1256). In contrary, the status update triggered by `syncTerminating` pods was just based on the container runtime `containerRuntime.GetPodStatus`.
2. Why does the container runtime not populate the IP information for stopped pods? 
Because of the explicit check for SANDBOX_READY [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/291378cd33cb89342fa876e201030172bb33d3b9/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L1460-L1462)
3. Why does the `podStatus` cache contains the IP information when `syncTerminatedPod` is called. Because it gets updated inside [updateCache](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae1859c896d742de1ee60a349475f8e28b61995/pkg/kubelet/pleg/generic.go#L432). Note that, in that case we also fallback to `oldPodStatus.IP` for stopped containers, see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae1859c896d742de1ee60a349475f8e28b61995/pkg/kubelet/pleg/generic.go#L424-L426).  
4. Are there more fields that need to be copied? 
It seems not. When calling `containerRuntime.GetPodStatus` on a stopped pod all fields except for [podStatus](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae1859c896d742de1ee60a349475f8e28b61995/pkg/kubelet/container/runtime.go#L307C3-L323) except for `IP` and `Timestamp` are returned. The `Timestamp` field seems only be used when storing in cache, see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae1859c896d742de1ee60a349475f8e28b61995/pkg/kubelet/pleg/generic.go#L478-L482), and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae1859c896d742de1ee60a349475f8e28b61995/pkg/kubelet/container/cache.go#L102-L117) . However, we don't store this status in cache.
5. Why copy the information at the `podStatus` (*kubecontainer.PodStatus) level, not at the `apiPodStatus` (v1.PodStatus) level?
Both would work, but adjusting the underlying structure is less code (single field vs two), and keeps them consistent as commented [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125404#discussion_r1634560821)
6. Is a more generic approach possible, rather than fixing a specific field? 
Possibly, we could fallback the IPs inside `generateAPIPodStatus` or `convertStatusToAPIStatus`, which also have access to `oldPodStatus`, containing the IPs, but this would affect many more code paths. The proposed fix is minimal to only fix the new status update introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115331/: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115331/files#diff-67dd9e8f3ee257072765326cb4f242852554a2c0753563fa51e292c0a63a7b94R2022
7. Why after the fix there is one less status update? Because kubelet skips sending status update if there is no difference (skips sending patch if empty inside [PatchPodStatus](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a4b8edd0f7131f0979d1f7168de1bfa5cb838d01/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L873)). The only difference between the 2 status updates triggered by `syncTerminatingPod` and `syncTerminatedPod` was the presence of the `IP` fields, so `syncTerminatedPod` is skipped.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix the bug where PodIP field is temporarily removed for a terminal pod
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:


```docs

```
evidence: Because of the explicit check for SANDBOX_READY, the container runtime does not populate the IP information for stopped pods.

root_cause_text: The bug occurred because the field PodIP.IP, which is used as a key in a list map in PodStatus.PodIPs, was not marked as a required field in the CRD OpenAPI schema. Kubernetes enforces that such key fields must be either required or have default values, and the absence of this requirement caused CRD validation to fail. This requirement was overlooked during schema generation, causing the issue.
fix_summary: Fixes a 1.30.0 regression in openapi descriptions of PodIP.IP  and HostIP.IP fields to mark the fields used as keys in those lists as required.
fix_pr_title: make PodIP.IP and HostIP.IP required.

Fields used as map keys must be required or defaulted when used in a CRD schema.

Fixes CRD generation for types that contain [PodStatus](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.30/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L4619)

```shell
spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[status].properties[podIPs].items.properties[ip].default: Required value: this property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, so it must have a default or be a required property
```



Fixes #124900
Supercedes #124904
xref #124540 

```release-note
Fixes a 1.30.0 regression in openapi descriptions of PodIP.IP  and HostIP.IP fields to mark the fields used as keys in those lists as required.
```

cc @tatsuhiro-t

root_cause_text: The root cause of the bug was that the removeMissingExtendedResources() function was incomplete in its processing scope; it only sanitized the extended resource requests of regular containers but neglected to perform the same cleanup for initContainers. Since initContainers can also request extended resources unknown to the node, this omission led to potential resource mismatches and pod admission failures.
fix_summary: Remove missing extended resources from init containers
fix_pr_title: Remove missing extended resources from init containers
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The function removeMissingExtendedResources() located at pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go:217, is designed to remove any extended resources from a container’s requests that are not found in nodeInfo.Allocatable before the pod is admitted. 
This is necessary to support cluster-level resources, which are extended resources that are unknown to nodes.
However, this function only removes missingExtendedResources from the container’s requests, and does not process the requests of initContainers. 
This could lead to issues, as initContainers might request resources that do not exist on the node, which could result in the pod failing to be admitted or other unforeseen issues.

root_cause_text: The root cause of the bug was that the Job was marked as Failed or Completed as soon as failure or success conditions were met, without waiting for all Pods to reach a terminal state. This caused running Pods to still be counted as ready, leading to inaccurate accounting in higher-level controllers that rely on Job conditions.
fix_summary:
Delay setting terminal Job conditions until all pods are terminal.

Additionally, the FailureTarget condition is also added to the Job object in the first Job
status update as soon as the failure conditions are met (backoffLimit is exceeded, maxFailedIndexes, 
or activeDeadlineSeconds is exceeded).

Similarly, the SuccessCriteriaMet condition is added in the first update as soon as the expected number
of pod completions is reached.

Also, introduce the following validation rules for Job status when JobManagedBy is enabled:
1. the count of ready pods is less or equal than active
2. when transitioning to terminal phase for Job, the number of terminating pods is 0
3. terminal Job conditions (Failed and Complete) should be preceded by adding the corresponding interim conditions: FailureTarget and SuccessCriteriaMet
fix_pr_title: Delay setting terminal Job conditions until all pods are terminal
fix_pr_body:

root_cause_text: The bug occurred because the mechanism that requeued Pods on pod add/update events filtered Pods only based on PodAffinity and resizing status, ignoring Pods rejected by PodTopologySpread. This selective event delivery prevented Pods rejected by PodTopologySpread and other plugins with similar event subscriptions from being requeued after pod-related events, causing them to get stuck unrescheduled.
fix_summary:
Fix a bug that when PodTopologySpread rejects Pods, they may be stuck in Pending state for 5 min in a worst case scenario.
The same problem could happen with custom plugins which have Pod/Add or Pod/Update in EventsToRegister,
which is also solved with this PR, but only when the feature flag SchedulerQueueingHints is enabled.
fix_pr_title: take PodTopologySpread into consideration when requeueing Pods based on Pod related events
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?





#### What this PR does / why we need it:

- AssignedPodAdded(): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1044
- AssignedPodUpdated(): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1069

When assigned Pods are created/updated, cluster events (Pod/Add or Pod/Update) should be delivered for all plugins that subscribe those events. But, actually `getUnschedulablePodsWithMatchingAffinityTerm` pre-filters Pods to receive those events based on Pods' affinity and `pod.Status.Resize`. - meaning only PodAffinity/NodeResourceFit receive them actually.

The problem here is similar to #110175 - in in-tree plugins, PodAffinity, PodTopologySpread and NodeResourceFit subscribe Pod add and/or update events. And, Pods rejected by PodTopologySpread will never be requeued to activeQ by Pod-related events. The same happens for custom plugins registering pod add and/or update events.

---

This PR addresses this problem by -

- take PodTopologySpread into consideration when requeueing Pods based on Pod related events.
  - This fix is mostly for people who don't use QHint enabled.
- use MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue only, when the feature gate is enabled.
  - It's the general fix to fix the same problem in custom plugins. We have to guard it with feature flag, otherwise negative impact on the throughput. (it's like we can't remove preCheck until QHint is done)


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #122626
Fixes #123480

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

@kubernetes/sig-scheduling-leads 
It **might** be a candidate for cherry-pick. I'm not sure and don't have a strong opinion.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix a bug that when PodTopologySpread rejects Pods, they may be stuck in Pending state for 5 min in a worst case scenario.
The same problem could happen with custom plugins which have Pod/Add or Pod/Update in EventsToRegister,
which is also solved with this PR, but only when the feature flag SchedulerQueueingHints is enabled.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:


```docs

```
evidence: `getUnschedulablePodsWithMatchingAffinityTerm` pre-filters Pods to receive those events based on Pods' affinity and `pod.Status.Resize`. - meaning only PodAffinity/NodeResourceFit receive them actually.

root_cause_text: The root cause is that the code generator (applyconfiguration-gen) does not handle the presence of multiple embedded structs that contain fields with the same name. This leads the generator to produce methods and field accesses that are ambiguous or duplicated because it does not qualify or differentiate these fields based on their embedding types. The defect is that applyconfiguration-gen assumes unique member names at the top level without considering embedded struct conflicts.
fix_summary: applyconfiguration-gen no longer generates duplicate methods and ambiguous member accesses when types end up with multiple members of the same name (through embedded structs).
fix_pr_title: Handle ambiguous fields in applyconfiguration-gen
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With embedded structs, objects can end up with conflicting members: members with the same name in different structs (embedded or not). These aren't ambiguous in Go, but applyconfiguration-gen's generated functions ignore this possibility and produce ambiguous member accesses and duplicate methods.

This resolves the problem by qualifying embedded member accesses with their types when appropriate, and by memoizing generated function names to avoid duplicates. When conflicting members are encountered, functions are generated for the first one; this is assumed to produce correct results.

For applyconfiguration-gen, a more correct approach would be to only generate With... and Get... functions for the specific members the generator is interested in; but that would be a breaking change for any client code relying on the other With... functions.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #126982

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
applyconfiguration-gen no longer generates duplicate methods and ambiguous member accesses when types end up with multiple members of the same name (through embedded structs).
```

```docs

```

root_cause_text: The Kubernetes grpc client for KMSv2 plugin communication sets the authority header in grpc requests to the Unix domain socket (UDS) file path. root_cause_text: The root cause of the memory leak was OpenTelemetry's delegating MeterProvider which, before a real implementation is set, tracks every instrument created without deduplicating repeated creations. This caused unbounded memory growth when instruments were created repeatedly, such as for grpc clients, leading to excessive memory consumption in kube-apiserver.
fix_summary: Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
fix_pr_title: Fix memory leak from global OpenTelemetry MeterProvider
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fix memory leak caused by https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go-contrib/issues/5190.  OpenTelemetry has a "delegating" MeterProvider that keeps track of instruments created using the API until a real implementation is added. However, it doesn't return existing instruments if the same instrument is created repeatedly, leading to a memory leak if repeatedly creating clients (grpc, in our case).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126918

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I've opted to use an init function to set this because we are overriding the global default.

I'm doing this in the kubelet and APIServer because there are other users of component-base/tracing on github that may be actively using the metrics portions of the OTel libraries, which would be broken by adding it to component-base.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixes a kubelet and kube-apiserver memory leak in default 1.29 configurations related to tracing.
```

root_cause_text: Kube-proxy was marking its initialization as complete before all service and endpointslice updates had been fully processed and delivered. This led to incomplete service state, causing transient removal of service rules and failure to clean up stale UDP conntrack entries.

root_cause_text: The root cause is that the endpoints controller relies on tracking the resource version of Endpoints objects to detect changes and avoid stale information. However, some update operations do not increment the resource version, resulting in the controller mistakenly treating those updates as stale and not reconciling the Endpoints properly, leading to endpoints staying out of sync.
fix_summary: Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
fix_pr_title: bugfix: endpoints controller track resource version conrrectly
fix_pr_body:
The endpoints controller store the resource version of the previous Endpoints objects to avoid issues related to stale information on the cache since https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125675

However, there can be update operations that succeed without increasing the resource version, causing the endpoints controller to declare stale the existing Resource Version and stopping the Endpoints to be updated.

Co-Author-By: Quan Tian <quan.tian@broadcom.com>
Co-Author-By: Yang Yang <yyyng@amazon.com>



Fixes #126578, #127370

```release-note
Fix a bug on the endpoints controller that does not reconcile the Endpoint object after this is truncated (it gets more than 1000 endpoints addresses)
```
evidence: There can be update operations that succeed without increasing the resource version, causing the endpoints controller to declare stale the existing Resource Version and stopping the Endpoints to be updated.

root_cause_text: When SidecarContainers feature is enabled, the code does not retry starting an init container if the initial StartContainer call fails and leaves the container stuck in Created state. root_cause_text: The bug happened because the eviction event message generation code omitted restartable init containers (sidecars) and init containers from the accounting of resource usage, resulting in inaccurate eviction messages and annotations. The logic only considered regular containers, failing to include these container types in the eviction resource consumption reporting.
fix_summary: Fixes a bug where restartable and non-restartable init containers were not accounted for in the message and annotations of eviction event.
fix_pr_title: [Sidecar Containers] Consider init containers in eviction message
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a Pod is evicted due to resources pressure on the node, the kubelet creates an eviction event and reports it to the user. The event message includes which containers within the Pod exceeded their resource requests, along with their actual usage. If a resource request is not set, it will always be reported as a violation. Similar information is also included in the event annotations.

Currently, the `evictionMessage` function, which generates the message and annotations for the eviction event, does not account for the init containers and restartable init containers (sidecar containers). Since the resources field cannot be specified for ephemeral containers, they will always be blamed for resource overuse when an eviction occurs. That’s why only regular, init and restartable init containers are considered for the eviction message.

This PR improves the eviction message to account for init and restartable init containers. When a Pod with both restartable init containers and regular containers gets evicted, here's what the output looks like:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
count: 1
eventTime: null
firstTimestamp: "2024-05-19T08:14:14Z"
involvedObject:
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  name: alloc-lm9sq
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "19979"
  uid: 786af1f6-3b04-4385-b61f-acfca78ddfd6
kind: Event
lastTimestamp: "2024-05-19T08:14:14Z"
message: 'The node was low on resource: memory. Threshold quantity: 1536Mi, available:
  1208704Ki. Container el1 was using 44Ki, request is 0, has larger consumption
  of memory. Container el2 was using 48Ki, request is 0, has larger consumption
  of memory. Container el3 was using 48Ki, request is 0, has larger consumption
  of memory. Container el-sidecar1 was using 3818464Ki, request is 0, has larger
  consumption of memory. Container el-sidecar2 was using 1452Ki, request is 0, has
  larger consumption of memory. Container el-sidecar3 was using 48Ki, request is
  0, has larger consumption of memory. '
metadata:
  annotations:
    offending_containers: el1,el2,el3,el-sidecar1,el-sidecar2,el-sidecar3
    offending_containers_usage: 44Ki,48Ki,48Ki,3818464Ki,1452Ki,48Ki
    starved_resource: memory
  creationTimestamp: "2024-05-19T08:14:14Z"
  name: alloc-lm9sq.17d0d5ba642ef84c
  namespace: default

reason: Evicted
reportingComponent: kubelet

  component: kubelet
  host: kind-worker

```

root_cause_text: The memory manager did not enforce the rule that a NUMA node cannot have both single-NUMA and cross-NUMA memory allocations simultaneously. This led to inconsistent admission decisions where pods violating this NUMA allocation policy could still be admitted, causing allocation failures and UnexpectedAdmissionError.
fix_summary: memorymanager: avoid violating NUMA node memory allocation rule
fix_pr_title: memorymanager: avoid violating NUMA node memory allocation rule
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?


#### What this PR does / why we need it:
According to https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation and to the design introduce in the memory manager KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1769-memory-manager the NUMA node can not have both single and cross NUMA node allocations.

There're cases when the chosen affinity hint does not align with the rule above but the pod get admitted anyway.

The implications are incosistent admission/rejection behaviors from memory manager side.

In order to fix the issue, we should validate that the affinity hint that has been chosen is not violating the above rule.

A detailed example for demonstrating the issue:
Available resources of `NodeA`
``` yaml
NodeA:
  NUMA0:
    cpu: 2
    memory: 1024 MBi
  NUMA1:
    cpu: 2
    memory: 1024 MBi
```
Upcoming pods:
```yaml
Pod1: #(Guaranteed)
  cpu: 1
  memory: 512 MBi

Pod2: #(Guaranteed)
  cpu: 2
  memory: 1280 MBi
```

t0: `Pod1` get admitted and lands on NUMA0
t1: current available resources state:
``` yaml
NodeA:
  NUMA0:
    cpu: 1
    memory: 512 MBi
  NUMA1:
    cpu: 2
    memory: 1024 MBi
```
NUMA0 marked by the memory manager as single NUMA memory allocation
 
t2: `Pod2` gets rejected (as expected) because it needs memory from both NUMAs in order to satisfy its request and NUMA0 already marked as a single NUMA group so it cannot serves allocation which spans across NUMAs.

But, assuming `Pod2` would request additional CPU:
``` yaml
Pod2 #(Guaranteed):
  cpu: 3 #(instead of 2)
  memory: 1280 MBi
```
t2: pod gets admitted which is inconsistent and violates the NUMA grouping rule.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #120733

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:


```docs

```
evidence:
"According to https://kubernetes.io/blog/2021/08/11/kubernetes-1-22-feature-memory-manager-moves-to-beta/#single-vs-cross-numa-node-allocation and to the design introduce in the memory manager KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1769-memory-manager the NUMA node can not have both single and cross NUMA node allocations.
There're cases when the chosen affinity hint does not align with the rule above but the pod get admitted anyway."

root_cause_text: The documentation incorrectly stated that the --cluster-cidr flag requires --allocate-node-cidrs to be true. In reality, the kube-controller-manager allows setting a non-empty --cluster-cidr with --allocate-node-cidrs set to false, ignoring the cluster cidr parameters in that case. The bug originated from documentation not accurately reflecting this conditional flag usage, leading to confusion.
fix_summary: Clarified the kube-controller-manager documentation for --allocate-node-cidrs, --cluster-cidr, and --service-cluster-ip-range flags to accurately reflect their dependencies and usage conditions.
fix_pr_title: Fix flag documentation kube-controller-manager and cloud-provider
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR solved issue #119066 

Currently, the documentation of the following kube-controller-flags flags are ambiguos:
```
--allocate-node-cidrs Should CIDRs for Pods be allocated and set on the cloud provider.
--cluster-cidr CIDR Range for Pods in cluster. Requires --allocate-node-cidrs to be true
--service-cluster-ip-range CIDR Range for Services in cluster. Requires --allocate-node-cidrs to be true
```
Both restrictions on `--cluster-cidr` and `--service-cluster-ip-range` regarding `--allocate-node-cidrs=true` are incorrect since it is possible to run `kube-controller-manager` with those flags together with `--allocate-node-cidrs=false`. 

Basically, `--allocate-node-cidrs=true` activates the controller `nodeipam` for which `--cluster-cidr` and `--service-cluster-ip-range` are *mandatory*.  However, if `--allocate-node-cidrs=false` , flags `--cluster-cidr` and `--service-cluster-ip-range` are *ignored*

Thus, the documentation of these flags is corrected to the following:

```
--allocate-node-cidrs Should CIDRs for Pods be allocated and set on the cloud provider. Requires --cluster-cidr.
--cluster-cidr CIDR Range for Pods in cluster. Only used when --allocate-node-cidrs=true; if false, this option will be ignored.
--service-cluster-ip-range CIDR Range for Services in cluster. Only used when --allocate-node-cidrs=true; if false, this option will be ignored.
```


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #119066

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Clarified the kube-controller-manager documentation for --allocate-node-cidrs, --cluster-cidr, and --service-cluster-ip-range flags to accurately reflect their dependencies and usage conditions.
```

root_cause_text: The root cause is that during node shutdown, the shutdown manager checks only for pod termination to proceed without ensuring that volumes used by these pods are successfully unmounted. Since volume teardown only starts after containers have stopped, there is a race condition where the CSI driver may be terminated or the OS may shut down before volumes are fully detached, leading to unclean unmounts and prolonged pod restarts.
fix_summary: Node shutdown controller now makes a best effort to wait for CSI Drivers to complete the volume teardown process according to the pod priority groups.
fix_pr_title: Ensure volumes are unmounted during graceful node shutdown
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?





#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR ensures that CSI drivers have the opportunity to perform necessary volume teardown during node shutdown, preventing data corruption and reducing pod restart times.

The current node shutdown manager and volume manager in Kubelet both operate off the same signal (termination of pods), which leads to the following race condition:

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/99845161/5f32e776-f370-4394-9586-8d17ddc0420c)
_Diagram as provided by @msau42_ 

#### Overview of changes
`VolumeManager` has been added as a dependency to the node shutdown controller (`nodeshutdown.Manager`) in Kubelet. This change allows for querying the status of volume mounts before proceeding with the termination of pods. Waiting for unmounts is done on a best effort basis - if the volume unmounting process fails, the error is logged, but the shutdown process continues.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #115148.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This PR builds on the work started in [#120091](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120091). Credit to [@mauriciopoppe](https://github.com/mauriciopoppe) for authoring the initial fix.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Node shutdown controller now makes a best effort to wait for CSI Drivers to complete the volume teardown process according to the pod priority groups.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

#115148

```docs

```
evidence: The current node shutdown manager and volume manager in Kubelet both operate off the same signal (termination of pods), which leads to the following race condition... Node graceful shutdown to also wait for volumes to be torn down.

root_cause_text: The bug happened because the Kubelet prematurely marked pods as terminated (Succeeded or Failed) in the API before all containers were fully stopped and prevented from restarting. This caused rapid repurposing of node resources and led to inaccurate 'OutOfCpu' errors on subsequent pods, due to resource accounting being inconsistent during quick pod turnover.
fix_summary: Fixed a 1.22 regression that could incorrectly reject pods with OutOfCpu errors if they were rapidly scheduled after other pods were reported as complete in the API. The Kubelet now waits to report the phase of a pod as terminal in the API until all running containers are guaranteed to have stopped and no new containers can be started.  Short-lived pods may take slightly longer (~1s) to report Succeeded or Failed after this change.
fix_pr_title: Delay writing a terminal phase until the pod is terminated
fix_pr_body:
Other components must know when the Kubelet has released critical resources for terminal pods. Do not set the phase in the apiserver to terminal until all containers are stopped and cannot restart.  Because the pod worker was inferring the transition to terminal state due to the propagation of the phase to the API and then back in from the config loop (which means that if the apiserver is down, failed and succeeded pods aren't torn down on the node), we need to instead have syncPod signal that the normal lifecycle of the pod has led to termination.

After those two changes, one of the init container tests was failing because TerminatePod was defaulting regular container status to the unknown error (137) even though we know for sure in this case no regular containers were ever started.  Correct TerminatePod defaulting to only include plausibly started containers (according to the pod lifecycle).  It's possible that the race that led to pods succeeding even though we never successfully ran the necessary containers is now fixed, but a future change will have to experiment with that.

Fixes #106884, #108733

The Kubelet now waits to report the phase of a pod as terminal in the API until all running containers are guaranteed to have stopped and no new containers can be started.  Short-lived pods may take slightly longer (~1s) to report Succeeded or Failed after this change.

root_cause_text: The garbage collector controller blocks indefinitely awaiting informer cache sync. When a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) has a broken conversion webhook causing its resources to fail listing or watching, informer sync fails, blocking the garbage collector controller initialization and causing it to be stuck. This defect arises because the controller does not handle cache sync failures gracefully for resources that cannot be properly listed or watched.
fix_summary: Fixes a bug in the garbage collector controller which could block indefinitely on a cache sync failure. This fix allows the garbage collector to eventually continue garbage collecting other resources if a given resource cannot be listed or watched. Any objects in the unsynced resource type with owner references with `blockOwnerDeletion: true` will not be known to the garbage collector. Use of `blockOwnerDeletion` has always been best-effort and racy on startup and object creation, with this fix, it continues to be best-effort for resources that cannot be synced by the garbage collector controller.
fix_pr_title: garbagecollector: controller should not be blocking on failed cache sync
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?





#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Follow-up from #120164 & #110858

Garbage collector controller should not block indefinitely on cache sync failure. This can specifically happen if there is a CRD with a broken conversion webhook that is causing the initial cache sync to fail (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/101078).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #101078

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixes a bug in the garbage collector controller which could block indefinitely on a cache sync failure. This fix allows the garbage collector to eventually continue garbage collecting other resources if a given resource cannot be listed or watched. Any objects in the unsynced resource type with owner references with `blockOwnerDeletion: true` will not be known to the garbage collector. Use of `blockOwnerDeletion` has always been best-effort and racy on startup and object creation, with this fix, it continues to be best-effort for resources that cannot be synced by the garbage collector controller.
```

```docs

```

root_cause_text: The eviction manager was implemented such that it always overrides the pod's original termination grace period with the configured maximum pod grace period for soft evictions, ignoring the pod's own specified grace period. This behavior contradicts the documented expected behavior where the kubelet should use the lesser of the pod's grace period and the maximum grace period configured for soft evictions. As a result, the grace period is incorrectly extended rather than bounded, leading to a longer-than-intended pod termination grace period.

root_cause_text: The system-validator logic assumed that if the kernel has cgroup v2 enabled, it should validate against cgroup v2 controllers. However, in scenarios where the kernel supports cgroup v2 but the user configures Kubernetes to use cgroup v1, the validator incorrectly fails because it checks cgroup v2 files and expects cgroup v2 controllers to be present. This mismatch causes validation failure even though the cgroup v1 configuration is valid.

- but the user want to use the cgroup v1 for kubernetes

root_cause_text: The service-lb-controller's event handlers were registered and invoked before the controller was fully initialized (specifically before the event recorder was set up), leading to a panic when handlers accessed uninitialized state. This happened because the handlers were added upon instantiation, but full initialization occurs later in the Run method, causing a use-before-initialization error.
fix_summary: Fixes a bug in the `k8s.io/cloud-provider/service`  controller, it may panic when a service is updated because the event recorder was used before it was initialized. All cloud providers should using the `v1.31.0` cloud provider service controller must ensure that the controllers is initialized before the informer start to process events or update it to the version 1.32.0.
fix_pr_title: cloud service controller stops reporting events in the informer's event handlers
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:

If kube manager is started with no cloud-provider, it looks like the service-lb-controller fails to be instantiated but its handlers are added to the informer on instantiation. A part of its initialization happens on the Run method. because the recorder is nil, the event handler will panic. 

The event handler shouldn't be registered. It is detected with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/50c12437604b0cd5a73514389409fc2fde8b91bd. I open another PR to fix it, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/128182

This PR removes the event recorder from event handlers.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #128121

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixes a bug in the `k8s.io/cloud-provider/service`  controller, it may panic when a service is updated because the event recorder was used before it was initialized. All cloud providers should using the `v1.31.0` cloud provider service controller must ensure that the controllers is initialized before the informer start to process events or update it to the version 1.32.0.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:


```docs

```
evidence: If kube manager is started with no cloud-provider, it looks like the service-lb-controller is instantiated but not started. However, part of its initialization happens on the Run method and its handlers are added to the informer on instantiation. So the handlers still run and it crashes when they do because there is stuff not initialized, like in this case, the event recorder.

root_cause_text: The scheduler's resource calculation logic incorrectly accounted sidecar container resource requests by only comparing max resource demands between init and regular containers, ignoring the summed resource requests of sidecar and regular containers together as required. This discrepancy caused underestimation of resource usage for pods with sidecars, violating the resource calculation formula defined in the Sidecars KEP.

fix_pr_title: [scheduler] calculate pod requests resources with sidecar containers
fix_pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?



#### What this PR does / why we need it:
As per [Sidecars KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/753-sidecar-containers/README.md#resources-calculation-for-scheduling-and-pod-admission), resources calculations for scheduling pods with sidecars is : Max ( Max( each InitContainerUse ) , Sum(Sidecar Containers) + Sum(Containers) ), but [scheduler logic](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2d31ec00273c34390ec77637fb4ff96234885bca/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L950-L951) is using Max(RegularContainers, InitContainers) to calculate resources.
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #127868

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Scheduler will start considering the resource requests of existing sidecar containers during the scoring process.
```

```docs

```

This causes certain options like 'nosuid' to be lost after remounting, resulting in the NFS volume not being mounted with the specified options if subPath is used.
fix_summary: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
fix_pr_title: fix: preserve options after remount for bind mounting
